flow.caption_zh: 西安大雁塔夜間音樂噴泉。狀似展翅起飛的大雁。

zh: 我們雁群一路自塞北南飛
自印度歸來的玄奘弘法
en: That autumn day
It must be the Zhenguan era of the Tang Dynasty?
We, a flock of geese, fly south all the way from the northern frontier
Passing through Chang'an
I wander alone, apart from the crowd, as I please
Bowing the head to listen
Xuanzang, returned from India, spreading the dharma
Scriptures heavy and deep, Sanskrit chants rising softly
My heart grows still, entering meditation
Suddenly, a flash of insight
Turned to stone, unexpectedly, into a tower

zh: 聆聽古老歌聲起自遠方
en: The years slip away, dust and wind come and go
Whenever the north wind begins to rise
The dusk hour, about to rain yet not yet raining
I will strain my eyes to look all around
Longing for the geese flying south
How to fly past a thousand mountains of drifting cloud
How to look down upon
The vast expanse of Jiangnan
A watery land of fine grass and soft sand
In the dusk
Listening to an ancient song rising from afar
On and off, intermittent------
In middle age, listening to rain aboard a traveler's boat
The river broad, clouds low, a lone wild goose cries into the west wind 」
Could that be my own cry?
Tonight
Fine rain patters on, the old city desolate and still
I know
Just like the many ages of the past
There will be someone within the tower's shadow
Listening to the rain
Letting a whole life run its course
Drop by drop until the break of dawn

points.zh:
南宋，蔣捷 《 虞美人，聽雨 》：
少年聽雨歌樓上，紅燭昏羅帳。
壯年聽雨客舟中，江濶雲低，斷雁呌西風。
而今聽雨僧廬下，鬢已星星也。
悲歡離合總無情，一任階前點滴到天明。

大雁塔名稱由來。玄奘所着《大唐西域記》中記載，他在印度所聞僧人「埋雁建塔」的傳說，解釋了西安大雁塔名稱的由來。傳說在印度摩揭陀國的寺院，和尚信奉小乘佛敎，可吃三淨肉，卽雁肉，鹿肉和犢肉。一天，有位和尚見天空飛來一群雁，便說:“今天大家都沒有東西可吃了，菩薩應該知道我們肚子餓呀!“ 話剛說完，一只雁便墜落在和尚面前。他驚喜交加，遍告寺内衆僧，都認爲這是如來佛在敎化他們，於是在雁落之處，埋雁建塔，稱之爲雁塔。玄奘在印度遊學取經期間 ( 629年至645年，卽唐朝貞觀年間 ) ，瞻仰了這座雁塔。回國後，在長安慈恩寺講經其間，爲了存放從印度帶回的經書，佛像和舍利，于652年在慈恩寺西院，建造一座仿印度雁塔形式的磚塔，名之爲雁塔。塔名前加一大字，代表大乘佛敎的意思。
points.en: The origin of the name "Big Wild Goose Pagoda." In the "Great Tang Records on the Western Regions" (大唐西域記) written by Xuanzang, he recorded a legend he heard from monks in India about "burying a wild goose and building a pagoda," which explains the origin of the name of Xi'an's Big Wild Goose Pagoda. According to the legend, at a monastery in the kingdom of Magadha in India, the monks followed Hinayana Buddhism and were permitted to eat the "three kinds of pure meat" — namely goose meat, deer meat, and calf meat. One day, a monk saw a flock of geese flying overhead and said, "Today we have nothing to eat — surely the Bodhisattva knows our hunger!" As soon as he finished speaking, a goose fell dead in front of him. Startled and delighted, he told all the monks in the monastery, and they all believed that the Buddha was teaching them through this. So, at the spot where the goose had fallen, they buried the goose and built a pagoda, calling it the Wild Goose Pagoda. During Xuanzang's travels to study and obtain Buddhist scriptures in India (from 629 to 645 AD, during the Tang Dynasty's Zhenguan era), he visited and paid homage to this Wild Goose Pagoda. After returning home, while lecturing on the scriptures at Ci'en Temple in Chang'an, in order to store the scriptures, Buddha statues, and relics he had brought back from India, he built a brick pagoda in 652 in the western courtyard of Ci'en Temple, modeled on the style of the Indian Wild Goose Pagoda, and named it the Wild Goose Pagoda. The character "Big" (大) was added before the name to signify Mahayana Buddhism.
